text: This shark may have been alive before the United States existed.
It's a Greenland shark. Arctic water, near freezing.
It grows about one centimeter a year.
For a century, nobody could tell how old they get. No growth rings. No hard bones to count.
Then, in 2016, scientists found a clock hidden in the eye.
The center of the eye lens forms before birth, and never changes.
They radiocarbon dated it in twenty eight sharks.
The biggest, five meters long, came out at about three hundred ninety two years.
The range is wide. Somewhere between 272 and 512 years.
Some scientists think that's too high. But even they say: well over two hundred.
And females only become mothers at around a hundred and fifty.
Verdict: solved. The oldest known vertebrate on Earth.
And one of them may still be out there, swimming.
